title: Discovery: Reliability & Multi-region Fallbacks with Stratus Financial
summary: Intro discovery focused on reliability, incident tolerance, multi-region routing and fallbacks. Customer runs sensitive payments workflows; primary concerns are failover SLAs, data residency, and predictable latency under burst. Discussed hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs and Redwood fallbacks, model variants, KV cache consequences, and runbook handoff. Agreed next steps: run a short benchmark, share security docs, draft proposed fallback policy and pricing for reserved capacity.
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2027-11-02 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Maya P (Redwood AE), Ethan C (Redwood SE), Lina G (Redwood CSM), Carlos R (Stratus CTO), Priya M (Head Eng), Jamal O (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto gen): Quick discovery on reliability needs; action items captured at end.

00:00 Maya (Redwood): Hi everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro  - I'm Maya, AE on the account, and with me is Ethan, our SE, and Lina from success. How are you all?
00:22 Carlos (Stratus): Good thanks. Real quick for context, we're Stratus Financial, we run payments routing and reconciliation for a set of retail partners. We're evaluating Redwood for chat + short-form generation for customer support and some fraud triage. main thing for us is reliability and incident tolerance  - can't have false positives or downtime during peak settlement windows.
00:40 Maya (Redwood): Totally understood. Today we'd like to walk through how Redwood handles failures, fallbacks, multi-region routing and SLA guarantees for hosted, dedicated, and private options. Ethan will jump into the tech details.
00:55 Ethan (Redwood SE): Great  - my goal is to understand your failure modes and show what we can do about them. quick question: what are your busiest hours and are they regional?
01:08 Priya (Stratus): Peak is 14:00-18:00 UTC, mostly North America but we have EU peak too. About 7-8k requests per minute at peak for the fraud triage endpoint, with spiky bursts during promos.
01:24 Maya: And latency targets  - SLOs?
01:27 Jamal (SRE): We aim for 99.9 P95 under 300ms for the triage call. Cost is second, but predictable latency is critical.
01:38 Ethan: OK that helps. For hosted we have multi-region endpoints and automatic routing, with fallbacks to model variants and regions when capacity or networking incidents occur. For Dedicated, you get reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and we still support cross-region fallback if you enable burst capacity. For Private, we hand over control but provide the same routing logic through our control plane if required.
02:02 Carlos: Quick clarification  - when you say fallback to "model variants", do you mean a smaller model that runs faster, or a different quantized version? How do you preserve quality?
02:16 Ethan: Good question. We have a policy system: primary model is full-precision; fallback can be either a quantized variant of the same arch or a smaller family model. Fallback rules are configured by route  - you can set strictness (e.g., prefer quality, prefer latency). We also do quick regressions against a small prompt set during fallback to detect major regressions. It's not perfect  - note transcription: sometimes we say K-V cash instead of KV cache in docs  - but we do prefix/KV cache preservation strategies so that session-level context isn't lost between model switches.
02:52 Priya: That regression test  - is it automated in production or a preflight?
02:57 Ethan: It's a lightweight online check we run as part of the fallback handshake for critical routes. acceptable thresholds are configurable; if the fallback fails the regression, we skip it and try next option or route to a warmer standby region.
03:14 Jamal: How does multi-region routing handle data residency? Our EU flows must not leave EU for compliance.
03:22 Maya: For hosted, we support region pinning at route level so EU requests stay in EU and never cross. For Dedicated and Private, you control the infra and can deploy only in the EU region. For cross-region fallbacks we can limit fallbacks to compliant regions only  - we won't cross boundaries if you disable cross-border failover.
03:46 Carlos: SLA  - do you publish uptime and latency SLAs for hosted?
03:51 Maya: Yes, hosted has a documented SLA for uptime (99.9 for standard tiers, higher for enterprise) and we have latency SLOs in our docs, but latency is not an SLA in the same way as uptime; for Dedicated we provide tighter latency commitments and custom SLOs in contracts. I'll follow up with the exact service-level doc link.
04:12 Priya: We need to see runbooks  - if Redwood region goes down how do you failover? is it automatic or do we need to trigger?
04:22 Ethan: There are two modes: automatic and manual. For automatic, smart routing will shift traffic to an allowed fallback region and optionally switch model variants. For manual, you can disable or re-route via the Console. Automatic failover has configurable grace windows and cooldowns to avoid flapping. We'll share an example runbook and a sample policy.
04:45 Jamal: What about state  - KV cache and session continuity during failover? I.e., if I'm streaming a session and we failover, do we lose the prefix cache and force full re-generation?
04:58 Ethan: In some cases, yes  - KV cache is stored per region and when you failover across regions there's an expected cold-start for KV. We mitigate with two patterns: 1) cross-region async replication for hot prefixes (you opt-in for sensitive routes), or 2) sticky sessions with weighted routing + limited cross-region fallback during active sessions. Both have cost implications.
05:27 Carlos: Could you quantify? if we enable cross-region replication what's the latency hit and cost?
05:33 Ethan: Replication is async; typical added tail latency is small (tens of ms) for reads but write replication adds network egress costs and storage. For cost, it's a percent uplift  - we'll send an estimated pricing sheet. For dedicated there are different options: local-only KV for lowest latency or cross-region replicate for higher resilience.
05:55 Priya: For Dedicated  - can we reserve capacity in two regions and have active-active?
06:01 Ethan: Yes, active-active is supported. You can run dedicated pools in two regions behind the smart router which does weighted balancing and failover. We recommend canary traffic to warm caches during deployments. There's a tradeoff: double reservation increases cost.
06:18 Maya: On the security side  - audit logs, KMS, SSO?
06:22 Priya: Also SOC 2 and ISO attestation required.
06:25 Lina (Redwood CSM): We have SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001. For hosted we provide audit logs; for Private you get full control including KMS/HSM integrations and private networking. For SSO we support SAML/SCIM for provisioning and RBAC for console/API.
06:44 Jamal: Does audit logging include per-token cost traces? we need to map queries to costs for chargeback.
06:50 Lina: Yes, Console has token-level cost breakdowns and per-route dashboards. We can show an example dashboard in the next demo.
06:58 Carlos: What happens on major incidents  - do you have an RTO/RPO for state? we care about durability of queued requests during region outage.
07:08 Ethan: For queued requests we try to drain and route; if the region is unreachable in a hard outage some in-flight requests will fail. We offer durable queueing optionally via our dedicated message buffer or you can integrate your own. RTO is part of the contract for Dedicated/Private. For hosted the typical recovery is within minutes with automatic reroute but not guaranteed to preserve every in-flight request.
07:40 Priya: Can we simulate datacenter/region failures for acceptance testing?
07:45 Maya: Yes  - we do scheduled resilience tests with customers (chaos runs) and we can support a POC to run simulated region failures and measure behavior.
07:56 Jamal: About monitoring  - do you expose tracing spans and metrics to our Prometheus/Grafana?
08:03 Ethan: We export metrics and traces. We have integrations to send traces to OTEL/Jaeger and metrics to Prometheus pushgateway or metric exporters. We'll include an example config.
08:18 Carlos: Competitors  - worth noting we also talked to MajorCloud AI and EdgeServe. MajorCloud's managed endpoints have simpler pricing but less flexible fallbacks; EdgeServe advertised on-prem inference but limited multi-region routing.
08:34 Maya: noted  - thanks.
08:38 Priya: On rollback/rollouts  - how do canary and A/B work with fallback policies?
08:44 Ethan: You can tie rollout policies to routing rules. Canary routes will direct a percentage to new model version; if we detect latency or quality regressions we automatically rollback. Also have automatic fallback to previous model family if error rates spike.
09:02 Carlos: For our legal team we need a paper trail of incidents. Do you provide incident reports?
09:08 Lina: Yes, for enterprise we provide post-incident reports with timelines, impact, and mitigation steps.
09:14 Jamal: A few gotchas  - our SREs want to ensure we don't get into a situation where a fallback model changes semantics and causes false positives. can you gate fallback to only minor quantization changes?
09:26 Ethan: Absolutely, you can restrict fallback to specific variant sets or disable fallback to smaller models; the router will then try region and capacity fallbacks first.
09:33 Priya: For the fraud model we also want deterministic inference  - same prompt should produce same output unless model updated. How do you ensure determinism across replicas?
09:43 Ethan: Determinism is tricky with batching and multi-replica nondet. We offer a deterministic mode for critical routes that disables certain optimizations like dynamic batching and uses pinned seeds; expect higher latency/cost.
09:58 Carlos: Ok  - let's talk next steps and POC scope. What would you propose?
10:03 Maya: Proposed: 2-week POC, run on Hosted initially to validate routing/fallbacks, include a simulated region failover test and a load test to your 8k rpm peak. We'll provide a small prompt set for regression checks. If results look good we can scope Dedicated active-active in two regions.
10:20 Priya: That sounds fine. pricing?
10:23 Maya: We'll send a POC pricing sheet (hosted credits + optional reserved burst capacity). For Dedicated we'll give reserved pricing separately.
10:31 Jamal: Action items we need: security checklist, SOC docs, runbook example, and a network diagram for how to pin EU traffic.
10:38 Lina: We'll send the security pack and a sample runbook + network diagram.
10:43 Ethan: I'll run a quick benchmark with a synthetic payload that matches your median token size and share results next week. can you share sample payloads and a small prompt set?
10:53 Priya: We'll share sample payloads and the prompt set by Friday.
10:58 Maya: Great. To recap: Redwood to run hosted POC with multi-region routing test, share security docs, provide benchmark and proposed fallback policy. Stratus to share payloads, confirm POC dates, and invite their legal/security to a follow-up.
11:15 Carlos: Sounds good, thanks all.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors  - e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache, "Major Cloud" vs "MajorCloud", and some speaker mislabels in auto captions. Natural speech present: interruptions at 02:16 and 04:45, filler words, and clarifications.
